The Weierstrass substitution parametrizes the unit circle rationally, converting every rational expression in sine and cosine into a rational expression in t.
Substitute all three formulas at once, simplify the resulting rational function, integrate in t, and then replace t by tangent of x over two.

items.text: The map misses x congruent to pi modulo 2pi, which corresponds to an infinite t. Split definite integrals at any such point rather than passing through it as an ordinary finite substitution.
Transform endpoints using the same continuous branch. Reversing or crossing a tangent branch without splitting can give wrong limits.
If the original integrand has a singularity, convergence must be checked as an improper integral; rationalization does not remove the need for that limit.

items.text: Do not forget the differential factor 2/(1+t squared).
For definite integrals, an endpoint at x = pi maps to an infinite limit and must be treated accordingly.
A single arctangent branch does not cover the whole real x-axis; keep the computation interval-local.
